metadata.source_prompt: A small underwater ROV with a camera to explore a lake

design.summary: Tethered ROV: 4 in sealed hull, 4 x T200 (surge, yaw, heave, roll), 6.1 kg, 239 g net lift, about 1.7 m/s, 18 min

uses: buoyancy foam (strapped to the top tubes)
PCA9685: PWM to the four ESCs (hangs under the tray)
four thruster cables, the tether and a vent plug through the rear end cap
forward camera behind the clear end cap
Raspberry Pi 5 (vehicle computer, Ethernet to the surface)
tether (coiled at the surface; its weight is carried there)
rail splices, the star ground and bus hubs

performance.cost_breakdown: parts 1743.75 USD, filament 21.85 USD (0.87 kg), fasteners ~6.60 USD, wiring 50.19 USD

assumptions: Seal the hull with fresh, greased O-rings and pull a vacuum through the vent plug (it must hold 10 minutes) before every dive; a flooded hull destroys the electronics.
Thrust is the maker's bollard figure interpolated to 14.8 V; drag uses Cd 1.0 on a 25 x 25 cm frontal area (a guess for an open frame) and leaves out the tether's drag.
Trim (foam and ballast) is computed for fresh water; in sea water it floats about 2.5 % more, so add one ballast weight.
The printed frame parts flood: they carry no pressure. PETG is fine in water; avoid PLA, which slowly swells.
